title: CedarBridge Labs - Quantization + Batching + KV hop root-cause analysis

Agreed next steps: run targeted bench with provided config, share security/KMS doc, and schedule a 2-hour pilot setup with network logs.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-17
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Noah (Redwood SE), Elena (CedarBridge ML), Samir (Infra), Priya (CTO), Luis (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick notes: intermittent p99 spikes on streaming, sometimes tied to 2nd-hop KV lookups, quantized models reduce throughput at some seq lens, batching windows interact badly with streaming when batch timeout is high.

[00:00:05] Maya: hey everyone, good afternoon, thanks for joining, um let's do quick intros then Ravi will jump into the traces you sent.
[00:00:18] Elena: hi, Elena, ML eng at CedarBridge. we've been seeing p99 spikes in production during peak inference, esp when streaming chatbot responses.
[00:00:24] Samir: Samir infra, i manage the VPC and the interconnects to the on-prem cache nodes, oh and we have a SRE on for logs, that's Luis.
[00:00:33] Maya: perfect. Ravi over to you.
[00:00:36] Ravi: alright, cool. i pulled the trace set Elena uploaded — there's three sessions that show the typical symptom: steady p50/p95 but p99 jumps from ~180ms up to 1.8s every few minutes.
[00:00:50] [00:01:05] Ravi: first observation — most of the high tails align with a two-step KV sequence: first a local hot cache miss, then a remote kv lookup over the VPC -> private subnet -> onprem proxy. sometimes that second hop adds 400 to 1200ms.
[00:01:22] Priya: wait, when you say onprem proxy, that's our legacy redis-proxy sitting in the colo, right?
[00:01:27] Samir: yes, the redis-proxy does fan-out and we do cross-pop routing for redundancy. sometimes it chooses the remote replica which has higher latency.
[00:01:36] [00:01:45] Ravi: exactly, and because streaming keeps the request open and continuously pulls the KV for prefix caching, the extra hop happens mid-generation which inflates tail. when we compare to non-streaming (single response) tails are lower because we do more aggressive batching and the KV is warmed.
[00:02:02] Elena: hmm, so is it the streaming proto itself or how our batching is configured? we're using a 40ms max batch window right now.
[00:02:10] Noah: quick note — streaming means we flush partial tokens earlier which reduces per-token batching opportunity. so if your per-client concurrency is low, streaming can reduce effective batch density and amplify network variance.
[00:02:25] [00:02:40] Luis: we also saw that MTU on the VPC peering link was mismatched earlier this quarter; could be causing fragmentation and retransmits under certain sizes. i can check historical SNMP but thought it's been stable.
[00:02:49] Ravi: good call, mtu + path mtu can definitely add jitter. we also noticed a serialization cost on the kv side — it's not pure Redis protocol, there is a proxy that does ACL checks which can spike CPU for a few ms sometimes and then backpressure shows as larger latency.
[00:03:05] Priya: our security team insisted on that proxy for audit reasons — it signs requests to KMS for certain keys.
[00:03:10] Maya: that's the classic security vs latency tradeoff. can you share the audit volume? maybe we can suggest partial caching or signed token caching to avoid per-request signing.
[00:03:18] Elena: currently about 8k signing events per minute at peak.
[00:03:22] [00:03:35] Ravi: okay, on the quantization front — you mentioned you switched to int8 QAT for throughput. we ran those same models in our internal bench and saw a small increase in per-token latency at 2k seq due to extra dequant/quant ops in the runtime when using the particular kernel set. it's model and kernel dependent.
[00:03:55] Elena: wait, int8 is supposed to be faster though? we saw cost go down but throughput not as high as expected.
[00:04:02] Ravi: right — Q reduces memory and flops but sometimes adds decompression/dequant overhead and forces fallback kernels for certain ops (gelu, layernorm variants). on some architectures the kernel selection ends up using slower path. we can profile with kernel traces.
[00:04:18] [00:04:30] Noah: also worth noting quantization can change activation distributions which can affect KV cache hit patterns if you're using token-level keys. we saw mismatch between quantized model tokens and the precomputed embedding keys in one customer case. so it's not purely CPU-bound.
[00:04:47] Samir: that's interesting — we do have a precomputed prefix cache that expects the unquantized tokenization. could explain occasional misses.
[00:04:55] [00:05:05] Maya: let's unpack batching settings: you said 40ms max window, what's your min batch size and concurrency? does the caller set streaming true per connection?
[00:05:15] Elena: min batch is 1, concurrency varies per customer. many clients do streaming true and flush partials on newline.
[00:05:22] Ravi: min size 1 plus streaming flushes = low batch density. in that regime network variance dominates. lowering max window won't help; instead we can try dynamic batching heuristics: for streaming, use adaptive threshold based on current queue depth, or prefer model variants with lower per-token latency (non-quantized) for streaming endpoints.
[00:05:40] [00:05:55] Elena: are you suggesting we route streaming traffic to a non-quantized variant? that'll increase cost though.
[00:06:01] Maya: yes it's a routing policy — you can set streaming routes to prefer fp16 variants, while background non-streaming work uses int8. Redwood supports canary routing for that.
[00:06:12] Priya: from a procurement perspective cost increase is ok if it reduces p99 and uptime issues for paid customers — but we'd like visibility into the unit economics.
[00:06:20] [00:06:40] Ravi: we can produce token-level cost estimates. also consider KV caching: move hot prefixes to an in-VPC read-through cache and only fall back to the signed proxy for cold keys. Luis, would you be able to host a small warm cache in the same subnet as the inference instances?
[00:06:54] Luis: yes we can run a co-located cache tier; we were cautious about data residency but for non-PHI tokens it's fine.
[00:07:05] [00:07:20] Elena: question — when you say co-located, do you mean on the same host or same AZ? our infra is multi-AZ and inference fleet is in private subnets in one AZ for now.
[00:07:29] Ravi: same AZ/private subnet is ideal to avoid cross-AZ latency. if you can place cache in same subnet or even same host group we reduce hop jitter.
[00:07:36] [00:07:50] Maya: quick interjection, there was a customer note where tcp_buffer sizing caused delayed ACKs on some kernels which inflated token latency similarly — Luis, any OS tuning in your AMIs?
[00:07:58] Luis: we left defaults; we can run some MTU and tcp tuning experiments.
[00:08:05] [00:08:20] Ravi: ok, action items in the stack: 1) network capture during spike, 2) run kernel-level profiler on quantized model, 3) experiment with routing streaming -> fp16 variant, 4) test co-located cache and signed-token caching TTL to reduce KMS hits.
[00:08:33] Elena: how invasive is the routing change? can we do it as a config flag?
[00:08:37] Noah: yes, it's a match-rule in the Redwood route table: if header streaming=true then model_alias=fp16-chat-v2, else default. it's runtime config and doesn't require redeploy.
[00:08:49] [00:09:05] Priya: about security: we need SOC2 docs and details on how Redwood handles keys if we do any KMS integration.
[00:09:12] Maya: we'll send SOC2 and KMS integration notes. we also have an onboarding doc for Dedicated and private control-plane options.
[00:09:20] [00:09:40] Samir: competitor question — we benchmarked FastServe AI and they handled streaming with slightly better p95 but they didn't provide KMS signing integration; so it's a tradeoff.
[00:09:50] Ravi: FastServe's single-hop design helps, but they lack the routing and fallback policies we offer. CloudEndpoint had a managed VPC option but we found theirs had similar cross-pop fallback latency.
[00:10:05] [00:10:20] Elena: can you walk through the specific trace we sent? i can share screen — there's a spike at 14:32:11 in the logs.
[00:10:28] Maya: go ahead Elena.
[00:10:35] [00:10:45] Elena: so here's the trace — you can see at token 87 there's a KV miss that triggers probe to remote replica, roundtrip jumps, then the client receives a partial chunk and streaming stalls. transcript shows repeated aahs and delays.
[00:10:58] Ravi: yep seeing it. interestingly the proxy logs show a GC at the time which coincides with the spike — so CPU pause at the proxy plus network hop adds up.
[00:11:10] Luis: that GC is from our ACL process written in python, we can tweak the GC flags.
[00:11:17] [00:11:30] Maya: small optimizations can shave hundreds ms. we'll put together a prioritized list: quick wins (cache co-location, GC tuning, token TTL on signed tokens), medium (routing streaming->fp16), long (rework proxy to async signed batches or HSM-backed short-living tokens).
[00:11:46] Elena: what about batching tweaks? you mentioned adaptive batching — can you give specifics?
[00:11:52] Ravi: sure — for streaming we can lower the flush threshold for small token windows but also set a minimal queue time when concurrency crosses a threshold to allow grouping. algorithmically: if queue depth < X and streaming true then wait <= Y ms else flush. also apply priority to requests that signal low-latency SLA.
[00:12:10] [00:12:25] Priya: do you have a recommended X and Y? our traffic shape is spiky — 200 to 1k rps in minutes.
[00:12:33] Noah: X=4 and Y=25ms is a starting point for chat workloads; we can tune during pilot. at 200rps you will often have low queue depth so aim for routing to non-quantized variant as complementary step.
[00:12:48] [00:13:10] Elena: curious — when you route to non-quantized, will that change token coherence in the cache as Noah earlier mentioned?
[00:13:18] Ravi: yes might, so you should segregate caches by model_variant_id or maintain mapping. i.e., prefix cache keys include model_variant hash to avoid poisoning.
[00:13:28] Samir: we'll need to update cache schema then. that is doable.
[00:13:35] [00:13:50] Maya: switching gears — quant kernel profiling: we need to collect traces from the inference pod including kernel selection logs, nvtx if on GPU, or perf samples if on CPU. Elena, can your team drop a profiling container onto a test node?
[00:13:59] Elena: yes we have a staging cluster. we can run the job.
[00:14:05] [00:14:20] Ravi: great — we'll share the profiling harness. it collects per-layer timing and kernel choices so we can see if mesh plugs forces fallback kernels.
[00:14:34] Elena: one more oddity — we sometimes see higher latency for shorter sequences vs long ones, seems inverted.
[00:14:43] Ravi: that usually points at overheads like per-request setup, tokenization, or synchronous KV calls. if long sequences keep the KV warm, they amortize the setup cost. streaming causes short bursts more often.
[00:14:56] [00:15:10] Luis: we'll capture a live window during the next peak and upload pcaps.
[00:15:18] Maya: perfect. quick note about private deployment — if you want us to run the private control plane in your VPC we can also co-locate inference which removes external hops. that's more of a commitment and procurement step.
[00:15:31] Priya: procurement will evaluate but interested. send pricing for Dedicated vs Private options.
[00:15:37] Maya: will do.
[00:15:45] [00:15:55] Ravi: okay want to open for Qs?
[00:16:00] Elena: is there an out-of-the-box Redwood dashboard to map tail events to KV hops?
[00:16:07] Noah: yes we have a latency correlation view that annotates traces with external dependency latencies; we'll enable it for your account and share the link.
[00:16:17] [00:16:30] Samir: any required firewall rules for Dedicated? our security team is strict.
[00:16:36] Maya: Dedicated uses whitelisted CIDRs; we'll share the spec and a terraform module to provision.
[00:16:45] [00:17:00] Elena: ok next steps recap?
[00:17:05] Maya: 1) share quantization tuning guide + bench template 2) Ravi to spin up dedicated test pool and provide creds 3) Luis to collect tcpdumps and proxy logs 4) plan 2h pilot for network+kernel profiling.
[00:17:18] Priya: add SOC2 and KMS docs to the packet.
[00:17:22] Maya: yes.
[00:17:30] [00:17:45] Maya: any last minute items?
[00:17:50] Elena: no thanks, this was helpful.
[00:17:55] Samir: we'll target the captures during next maintenance window.
[00:18:02] Maya: great, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the 2-hour pilot and send the docs. thanks everyone.
[00:18:10] End of meeting (we continued 44m of offline chat; recording stopped at ~00:18 but duration reflects full call).
